basis: Infection-associated microangiopathic hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and renal injury define HUS; neurologic injury and destructive intestinal complications occur in <30%.
Acute hepatitis C is a viral infection of the liver; progression to chronic hepatitis is a separate disease stage.
Inherited Parkinson disease causes degeneration of central motor pathways; no other organ involvement established.
Vertebral and epiphyseal dysplasia with premature osteoarthritis defines this skeletal disease umbrella.
An inherited immunodeficiency defined by defective T-cell responses; no additional organ damage is established.
Inherited degeneration of retinal cones and rods causes visual impairment.
Malignant tumor originates in the adrenal cortex, an endocrine gland; metastatic sites are not defining organ involvement.
Autoimmune neuromuscular-junction dysfunction affecting extraocular muscles; ptosis and diplopia do not establish intrinsic eye damage.
Smooth muscle malignancy arising in the breast; breast is outside the axes, and smooth muscle origin does not establish skeletal muscle disease.
Inherited trigeminal autonomic headache disorder; rhinorrhea, ptosis and other autonomic signs do not indicate additional organ damage.
Sandfly-transmitted viral febrile illness; transient systemic symptoms do not establish organ damage.
Central neurodegeneration causes parkinsonism, apraxia and cognitive impairment; motor manifestations do not establish primary muscle damage.
Branched-chain amino acid metabolic disorder; developmental and cognitive impairment from neurotoxicity is common, approximately >=30%, despite fewer acute crises.
PSEN1-associated early-onset Alzheimer disease causes cerebral neurodegeneration and dementia.
Microcephaly, severe developmental impairment, epilepsy and neonatal diabetes define the syndrome; renal, skeletal and optic abnormalities are <30%.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with azoospermia and male infertility; reproductive dysfunction without established endocrine gland dysfunction.
Autoinflammatory syndrome defined by inflammation of skin and subcutaneous fat; no additional common organ damage is established across subtypes.
AQP4-antibody-mediated disease targets the CNS and optic nerves, producing myelitis, brain lesions and optic neuritis.
Inherited red-cell aplasia; atrial septal defect and pulmonic stenosis occurred in 1/1 annotated patient, supporting cardiac involvement with limited frequency evidence.
Inherited amino acid transport disorder causing cerebellar dysfunction; vertigo is central, and photophobia or vomiting does not establish eye, ear or gut damage.
Metaphyseal cartilage and bone dysplasia, classified under Pyle disease; no additional organ involvement established.
Late motor-neuron dysfunction after polio, without active infection; weakness is neurogenic, while muscle atrophy and respiratory insufficiency are each <30%.
Inflammation directly affects the iris; anterior uveitis is predominantly immune-mediated, although infectious and traumatic causes also occur.
Female genital prolapse is a reproductive support disorder; urinary-organ prolapse in some subtypes does not establish common urinary damage across the umbrella.
Neurodevelopmental and severe orthopedic abnormalities define it; heart and urinary malformations each occur in 30-79%; ocular findings omitted at the four-axis cap.
